Body HTML:
Residential and light commercial boilers: modulating condensing, cast iron atmospheric, and combination units that produce both heating and domestic hot water. From 85,000 through over 200,000 Btu/h.

Condensing boilers run at 90%+ by returning water cool enough to condense the flue gas, and that is the catch worth understanding — a condensing boiler connected to a high-temperature cast iron radiator loop returning water at 160°F never condenses and never reaches its rated efficiency. It needs low return temperature, which means radiant floor, panel radiators sized for lower water, or an outdoor reset control.

Cast iron boilers tolerate high return temperature and rough water, last decades, and are the right answer on an old gravity-converted system. They also require a bypass or mixing arrangement to protect against thermal shock.

Check whether a pump is included: 27 of the units here ship with no circulator and 14 include a Grundfos. Combi units size the domestic side by flow, so a combi that heats the house adequately can still be short for two showers.

All 90%+ units need PVC, polypropylene or stainless venting plus a neutralized condensate drain.

Brands include US Boiler, Navien and IBC. Shop by brand: Burnham boilers, Navien boilers and Navien combi boilers.

Frequently asked questions

Condensing or cast iron boiler?

A condensing boiler reaches 90%+ only with low return water temperature, such as radiant floor or an outdoor reset control. A cast iron boiler tolerates high return temperature and suits older high-temperature radiator systems.

Does the boiler include a circulator pump?

Check the product title. Many listings say Includes Grundfos Pump or No Pump Included. If no pump is included, add one from circulator pumps.

What size boiler do I need?

Size the boiler from a heat-loss calculation for the building, not from the rating of the old boiler. Older boilers were often oversized.

It includes IBC SL G3 fire tube boilers from 85,000 to 260,000 BTU input and the VX series, and US Boiler (Burnham) Aspen fire tube boilers, with efficiencies of 95 to 96 percent and elevation ranges up to 10,000 or 12,000 feet.

Frequently asked questions

Why does a condensing boiler need low return water temperature?

It only condenses flue gas, and reaches its rated efficiency, when return water is cool enough. Radiant floors, low-temperature emitters and outdoor reset controls help.

Does a condensing boiler need a condensate neutralizer?

The condensate is acidic, so most installations need a drain and a neutralizer. See condensate neutralizers.

What venting does a condensing boiler use?

Sealed-combustion condensing boilers vent in PVC, CPVC, polypropylene or stainless, as the manufacturer lists. Check the maximum vent length for your model.

Combination boilers that provide both space heating and domestic hot water from one wall-hung unit. The collection includes IBC CX combi boilers at 150,000 and 199,000 BTU with 10:1 turndown, IBC SFC combi boilers from 125,000 to 199,000 BTU at 95% efficiency, and Navien NCB and NFC high-efficiency condensing combi boilers.

Size a combi boiler by both the heating load and the peak hot water demand, since domestic hot water flow usually drives input. Check the minimum firing rate for small zones, venting options, condensate disposal, and the gas line size. Confirm whether a system pump is included.

See also: Condensing Boilers, Water & Space Heating Units (Combi), Navien, Navien Combi Boilers, Navien Boilers.

Frequently asked questions

How do I size a combi boiler?

Check two numbers: the heating input must cover the heat loss, and the hot water side must keep up with the fixtures that run at the same time. Hot water demand usually sets the input.

Combi boiler or boiler with an indirect tank?

A combi saves space because there is no tank. A boiler with an indirect water heater stores hot water and handles several fixtures at once more easily.

Is a system pump included?

It depends on the model. Check the product title and specifications before ordering.

A Navien combi boiler heats the home and makes domestic hot water on demand from one wall-hung condensing appliance, so there is no separate water heater or indirect tank. We stock two series. The NCB-H (NCB-240/110H and NCB-240/130H) pairs 110,000 or 130,000 BTU/h of heating input with 199,900 BTU/h for hot water. The larger NFC-H (NFC-250/175H and NFC-250/200H) offers 175,000 or 199,900 BTU/h of heating with 210,000 BTU/h for hot water.

How to choose a Navien combi

Size it by two numbers. The heating input should cover the building's calculated heat loss, and the hot water side has to keep up with the fixtures that run at the same time. A combi that heats the house well can still be short for two showers at once, so check the hot water flow at your temperature rise. Plan for PVC, CPVC or polypropylene venting, a condensate drain with a neutralizer, and a gas line sized for the full input.

Compare every model side by side in the Navien model comparison. See also all Navien boilers, including heating-only NHB and NFB models, combi boilers from other brands, condensate neutralizers and Navien parts and vent kits.

Shop by model: NCB-240/110H, NCB-240/130H, NFC-250/175H and NFC-250/200H.

Frequently asked questions

What is the difference between the NCB-240/110H and the NCB-240/130H?

Both have 199,900 BTU/h of input for hot water. The NCB-240/110H has 110,000 BTU/h of heating input and the NCB-240/130H has 130,000 BTU/h.

NCB-H or NFC-H?

The NCB-H covers most homes. The NFC-H is the larger fire-tube combi, with 175,000 or 199,900 BTU/h of heating input and 210,000 BTU/h for hot water.

Can a Navien combi replace my boiler and water heater?

Yes. A combi heats the home and makes domestic hot water on demand from one wall-hung unit. Size it for both the heat loss and the fixtures that run at the same time.

Controls and ignition: aquastats and immersion wells (Honeywell/Resideo L8148E, L4006, L4008 and others), gas valves, ignition modules, pilot assemblies, thermocouples and thermopiles, oil burner controls and low water cut-offs.

Water side and safety: boiler pressure relief valves, boiler fill and feed valves, expansion tanks, air separators and air vents, boiler drains, temperature and pressure gauges, magnetic dirt filters and complete boiler trim kits.

Circulators: fixed and variable speed circulator pumps from Taco, Grundfos and others, including direct replacements for the Taco 007 and Grundfos UPS15-58.

Brand parts: factory US Boiler / Burnham parts plus parts for Weil-McLain and other major boilers.

Before you order, check the boiler's model and serial number on the rating plate and compare the old part's number, voltage and connection size. Gas valve, ignition and burner work should be done by a qualified heating technician. Not sure what you need? Our zone valve replacement guide and the free Zone Planner can help, or contact us with your part number.

Navien replacement parts and accessories for tankless water heaters, combi-boilers and boilers. Complete units are not included here. The range covers concentric vent terminations, elbows, extensions, wall flanges and roof flashing, series parts kits, Ready-Link racks and primary manifolds, NaviLink Wi-Fi control, outdoor and temperature sensors, cascade cables, switching relays, the NaviClean magnetic filter and PeakFlow anti-scale systems.

Most of these parts are model-specific, and some are specific to a serial range. Navien revises components without changing the appliance name, so order from the data plate rather than from the model family. A vent kit for an NPE is not an NCB kit.

Venting accounts for many service calls. A concentric vent carries intake and exhaust in one pipe, so one damaged termination or cracked flange takes the unit out of service. Terminations have code and manufacturer clearances from windows, doors, soffits and property lines. A replacement in the same hole may no longer comply if the building has changed, and reusing an old gasket in a concentric joint is a common source of condensate leaks.

Can I replace a gas valve or safety control myself?

An indirect water heater makes domestic hot water using heat from a boiler. Hot boiler water circulates through a coil inside the tank and heats the potable water around it, so the tank has no burner of its own. Paired with an efficient boiler, an indirect tank can deliver a large supply of hot water.

This collection includes the indirect water heaters we carry from several brands. IBC tanks use 444 stainless steel and come with an aquastat, in sizes from 26.8 to 119 gallons, including the DTI-40, DTI-55, DTI-65 and DTI-80 models. AquaFlow indirect-fired water heaters are made of stainless steel in 30 to 119 gallon sizes. Heat-Flo offers 30 and 40 gallon indirect tanks with top connections, plus a 60 gallon high-output model with an element.

Size the tank to peak hot water demand and to the boiler output available for the domestic hot water zone. Confirm the coil connections and the boiler supply temperature, and decide whether the tank will be piped as a priority zone. Install a T&P relief valve, and a thermostatic mixing valve where required.

Shop boilers, all Heat-Flo products, mixing valves and water heater T&P relief valves.

Frequently asked questions

How does an indirect water heater work?

Hot water from the boiler runs through a coil inside the tank and heats the potable water around it. The tank has no burner or flue of its own.

What size indirect water heater do I need?

Size it to peak hot water demand and to the boiler output available for the hot water zone. Check the first hour rating and the coil connections.

Does an indirect tank need an anode rod?

Stainless steel tanks such as AquaFlow need no sacrificial anode. Check the product details for other brands.

Body HTML:
A circulator moves water around a closed loop rather than lifting it from a source, so it is sized for flow and head loss through the piping, not for pressure. Get the sizing wrong in either direction and the symptoms show up as noise and short-cycling when oversized, or as cold zones at the end of the run when undersized.

Fixed-speed circulators run at one curve and are matched to the loop at installation. Variable-speed and ECM circulators sense pressure differential and throttle themselves, which matters most on systems with zone valves where the flow demand changes as zones open and close — and they draw a fraction of the wattage of a comparable fixed-speed unit.

Cast iron bodies are for closed hydronic loops only; the oxygen in fresh water will corrode them. Any open loop or potable application — domestic hot water recirculation, for instance — needs a stainless steel or bronze body.

Most residential circulators use the standard flange bolt pattern, so replacing one is usually a matter of matching the flange spacing and the electrical supply.

Shopping by brand? See Taco circulator pumps or the full Taco Comfort Solutions range of pumps, cartridges and hydronic controls.

Body HTML:
Zone valves, actuators, dampers and panels for hydronic and forced-air zoning: 2-way and 3-way valves, fan coil valves, high-head models, replacement heads, zone dampers, forced-air panels and repair parts.

Zoning a hydronic system with valves instead of separate circulators is cheaper and simpler, but it changes the hydraulics: as zones close, flow through the remaining ones rises and the pump rides up its curve. That is why a valve-zoned system usually wants a pressure-bypass or a variable-speed circulator, and why a fixed-speed pump on a multi-zone valve system is often the source of velocity noise.

Most residential zone valves fail at the powerhead, not the valve body. Replacement heads are stocked separately and swap without draining the system, which is the cheap fix when a zone stops responding but the valve still moves by hand.

Connections are sweat, press, flare and FNPT in 1/2" through 1".

Brands include Resideo, Taco, Caleffi and Viega.

Popular part numbers: Honeywell V8043A1011, Honeywell V8043E1137, Honeywell 40003916-021, Honeywell VCZZ1100, Honeywell VU842A1046.

Taco Zone Sentry, QuickTop and 570 series valves are in Taco zone valves. For Taco pumps, switching relays and air vents, see Taco Comfort Solutions.

Frequently asked questions

Can I replace just the zone valve head?

Often, yes. If the valve body still opens and closes by hand, a replacement head fixes the zone without draining the system.

Normally open or normally closed?

A normally closed valve stays shut until the thermostat powers it open. A normally open valve stays open until it is powered closed. Match the old valve.

What does the end switch do?

The end switch closes when the valve is fully open and tells the boiler or circulator to run. Pick a valve with an end switch if the old one had one.

Are Honeywell and Resideo zone valves the same?

Yes. The V8043 and VC lines are now made by Resideo under the same numbers. See Honeywell Home and Resideo.

This collection covers Resideo aquastat controls and immersion wells for boilers and water heaters. It includes L4006A immersion aquastats with 100 to 240 degree ranges, L6006C surface-mount high and low limit controllers, L6008A low limit controllers with capillary, copper immersion wells in 1/2 and 3/4 inch NPT, and heat conductive grease.

Decide whether the control must break on rise as a high limit or make on fall as a low limit, and check the switching action, such as SPDT or SPST. Match the well size and insertion depth to the tank tapping and the control bulb, and apply conductive grease for accurate sensing. Confirm the setpoint range covers the application.

See also: Low Water Cut-Offs, Temperature Gauges, Controls, Switches & Sensors.

Popular part numbers: Resideo L8148E1299, Resideo L4006E1125, Resideo L4008E1156, Resideo L6006C1018, Resideo L7224U1002, Resideo 120650.

Frequently asked questions

How do I choose a replacement aquastat?

Match the part number on the old control, such as L8148E1299 or L4006E1125. If that number is discontinued, match the function (high limit, low limit or circulator), the temperature range and whether it needs a well.

Can I reuse the existing immersion well?

Usually, if the new control has the same bulb size and insertion depth. Add heat conductive grease to the well so the sensor reads the water temperature correctly.

Is a Resideo aquastat the same as a Honeywell aquastat?

Yes. Resideo makes the Honeywell Home aquastat line under the same model numbers. See all Resideo controls.

A boiler fill valve (also called a boiler feed valve or pressure reducing valve) keeps a hydronic heating system at the right cold-fill pressure, usually 12 to 15 psi for a typical two-story home. It automatically adds make-up water when pressure drops and lets you fast-fill the system after service. If your boiler pressure keeps falling, the fill valve never shuts off, or the relief valve drips, a worn or clogged fill valve is a common cause.

This collection lists fill and feed valves by part number, including Caleffi AutoFill 553 and 573 series (with or without gauge, NPT, sweat and press connections), the Caleffi 573/574 COMBO models with a built-in backflow preventer, Resideo NK300S and FM911 feed valve and backflow combinations, and Taco 329 fast-fill and 335 boiler feed valves. Replacement cartridges are listed where available.

Many local codes require a backflow preventer on the boiler fill line. A combination valve saves space and two joints. Match the inlet and outlet size (1/2" or 3/4"), connection type and pressure range to your system, and check whether your boiler needs an ASSE 1012 or 1013 backflow device.

Shop the rest of the hydronic water side in Boiler Parts, or go straight to relief valves, expansion tanks, backflow preventers and system fill tanks.

Frequently asked questions

Cast iron or stainless steel Grundfos circulator?

Use cast iron on closed hydronic heating loops. Use bronze or stainless steel for potable water and hot water recirculation, such as the UPS26-99SFC.

How do I pick the right flanges for a Grundfos pump?

Match the flange or union set to the pump model and the pipe size. See pump flanges.

How do I size a circulator?

Size the pump from the flow and head loss of the loop, not from pressure. An oversized pump is noisy and an undersized one leaves cold zones. See all circulator pumps.
